Comms and calendar

Comms and calendar

Draft templated email, preview recipients, send via outbox, and manage calendar invites — with Campaign vs History surfaces so ops never crowd the wizard.

Where comms live

Open Admin → Comms. The page has two surfaces:

  • Campaign (default) — the send wizard only: Audience → Message → Review → Send. Delivery log and calendar-invite tools are not on this surface.
  • History — delivery log (jobs, recipients, status) and calendar invite generate/update for scheduled sessions.

Deep-link with ?surface=history when you need the log or ICS panels. Send still enqueues outbox work for asynchronous drain — the request path does not call the email provider directly.

Campaign wizard

  1. On Campaign, set audience (status, search, or explicit selection). Next needs at least one recipient.
  2. Message — edit subject and body (merge fields like {{name}}). Click Save template before Next; the step stays blocked with “Save template before review” while unsaved.
  3. Review — run preview; inspect recipients, bodies, and missing fields. Editing audience or message invalidates a prior preview.
  4. Send (last step) — optional attach of an existing calendar invite, then Send. Trust-before-send: Send stays disabled without a valid matching preview.

Draft and preview

Preview requires a saved templateId on the server. Inspect missing fields before any send. Fix person or session data when required tokens are blank. Calendar invites (ICS with stable UID/SEQUENCE) are generated on History; on the hosted demo, email carries no attachments and speakers download the .ics from the portal instead. On Send you may attach an already-generated invite to this campaign.

  1. Open Admin → Comms (Campaign).
  2. Audience → Message → Save template → Review → Run preview.
  3. Repair data or template tokens until missing fields are acceptable.
  4. Send, then open History for the delivery log if you need job detail.

Scopes and CLI

comms:draft allows preview automation. comms:send is default-deny on new API keys and required for send. Agents should draft and show humans a preview before any key with send is used in production.

speakerops comms templates --event <eventId> --json
speakerops comms draft --template <templateId> --preview --json
speakerops comms send --preview-id <previewId> --json

Delivery backends

Local and many dev paths use sandbox provider behavior. Demo uses Cloudflare Email Sending, which delivers no attachments — calendar .ics files reach speakers as a portal download. Other environments may use Resend (attachment-capable) when EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend and secrets are set. Operators should know which provider the current host uses before debugging inbox issues.

WARNING. Never put raw API keys or magic links into template bodies. Prefer product tokens and portal links that require auth.

Where this lives in the app

  • /admin/comms

Open these routes on your demo or local host while you follow the steps above.
